explanation: It may keep a favourite stone in a loose pouch of skin under its foreleg, along with food it has gathered. Its dense fur keeps it warm without blubber.

claims.text: Sea otters float on their backs and use stones to crack open shellfish.
Walruses, harbour seals and manatees do not use stones as tools.
Sea otters can store a stone and food in loose pouches of skin under their forelegs.
Sea otters rely on very dense fur, not blubber, for insulation.
